content.text: {"condition":"Exercise-induced hypoglycemia","evaluationParameters":["Continuous glucose monitor readings before, during, and for several hours after cycling (including overnight for delayed hypoglycemia)","Recurrence and severity of hypoglycemia symptoms (sweating, tremor, difficulty concentrating) on cycling versus noncycling days"],"missingInformation":["Type, dose, and timing of insulin relative to the cycling session","Timing, composition, and carbohydrate content of the preexercise meal or snack","Preexercise CGM value and glucose trend arrow before starting the ride","Intensity of cycling (heart rate, perceived exertion) and whether it is steady-state aerobic","Occurrence of nocturnal hypoglycemia on cycling days","Client's hypoglycemia awareness and prior episodes","Whether fast-acting carbohydrate is carried during rides"],"priorityActions":["Treat acute hypoglycemia with 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose in 15 minutes, repeating until glucose is above 70 mg/dL","Consume 15–30 g of additional carbohydrate before cycling and/or reduce the preceding bolus/basal insulin dose on exercise days per provider protocol","Instruct client to carry fast-acting carbohydrate and glucose meter during rides and to check CGM before, every 30 minutes during, and after exercise"],"reasoning":"The client has type 1 diabetes with adrenergic and neuroglycopenic symptoms (sweating, tremor, difficulty concentrating) plus CGM-confirmed glucose of 58–64 mg/dL occurring only during or within one hour after cycling, while noncycling glucose is normal. No illness, ketones, or DKA features are present, and insulin/meals were not adjusted for the new exercise routine. This pattern is classic for exercise-induced (activity-related) hypoglycemia caused by increased insulin-mediated glucose uptake during aerobic exercise without a compensatory carbohydrate increase or insulin reduction.","stage1Confidence":"high","stemEvidence":[{"stemFact":"Client with type 1 diabetes","target":"condition"},{"stemFact":"Sweating, tremor, and difficulty concentrating during the ride or within one hour afterward","target":"condition"},{"stemFact":"CGM readings were 58–64 mg/dL on cycling days","target":"condition"},{"stemFact":"Noncycling fasting and premeal glucose 95–140 mg/dL","target":"condition"},{"stemFact":"Continued preexisting meal and insulin plan without an exercise-day adjustment","target":"priorityAction2"},{"stemFact":"Began a new 45-minute cycling routine after work","target":"priorityAction2"},{"stemFact":"CGM readings 58–64 mg/dL with hypoglycemic symptoms","target":"priorityAction1"},{"stemFact":"Symptoms recurred on three cycling days","target":"evaluationParameter2"},{"stemFact":"CGM already in use with readings 58–64 mg/dL during/after exercise","target":"evaluationParameter1"}]}
